neighbours.label: a word saying that something is everywhere or very ordinary (ubiquitous, common, staple, basic, abundant)
fire: Plastic bags are a ubiquitous sight along the highway.
Rice is a staple food in much of southern Asia.
Oxygen is one of the most common elements in the rock.
Smartphones have become commonplace in rural villages.
This widespread weed grows in almost any garden.
Bread is such a basic food that few think about it.
Sparrows are abundant in nearly every town here.
Coffee is an everyday habit for most of the staff.
quiet: Plastic bags are a strange sight along the highway.
Rice is a costly food in much of northern Europe.
Platinum is one of the rarest elements in the rock.
Smartphones have become unaffordable in rural villages.
This delicate orchid grows in only one garden.
Saffron is such a precious spice that few can buy it.
Sparrows are scarce in nearly every town here.
Coffee is an occasional treat for most of the staff.

notes: Card: ' ubiquitous' x7, ' common' x7, ' staple' x3, ' basic' x2, ' abundant' x2. Probes: ubiquitous 0.910, 'most common element' 0.860 (peak ' universe'), staple 0.653, basic 0.412; 'a rare sight' 0.059, 'most expensive' 0.083. New words (everyday, widespread, commonplace) are in the test to test the pattern. Near misses use the opposite or an unrelated adjective.
